headline: LEVI'S SPENT FOUR HOURS OF FILMING ON EVERY SECOND OF ITS CHRISTMAS ADVERT, E.L.F. BUILT ITS FIRST EVER HOLIDAY CAMPAIGN BY HAND, AND THE BIGGEST MATCHED TEST ANYONE HAS PUBLISHED SAYS CREATIVE MADE BY A MACHINE PERFORMS THE SAME
deck: Three brands put visibly handmade work on the air inside six days.  Levi's shot a claymation yeti at four hours of filming per finished second.  E.l.f. made its first ever holiday campaign entirely in stop motion and counted the women who built it.  Prada hired a Disney animator to draw by hand.  Not one of them says the word AI.  And the one large test that has run machine-made and human-made creative against each other, same advertiser, same campaign, same day, found no difference once the matched pairs are controlled for.  So the craft is not being bought for performance.  Work out what it is being bought for before you price it.
tldr: Levi's spent four hours of filming on every second of its claymation Christmas advert and e.l.f. built its first ever holiday campaign entirely by hand, while the largest matched test ever published found machine-made and human-made creative statistically equivalent, with the penalty attaching to looking machine-made rather than being it.  Write the proof of effort into your next creative brief as a deliverable with its own edit and its own release date, because the audience cannot see four hours per second and can only be told.

TikTok Shop has shipped a 14-day sales window for brand livestreams that sums four components across three attribution windows, names a model for only one of them, runs no control group, and emails the total to brand leadership on a recurring schedule.  Fix one attribution window for every channel in your holiday review this week and get the direct-sales figure in front of your leadership alongside the 14-day one, labelled.

A paid advert inside ChatGPT returned 89 cents a visit against 2 dollars 45 from paid Google search, converting at 0.37 percent against 1.17 with baskets 74 dollars smaller, and the biggest known buyer is paying 1 dollar 72 for a click the researchers price at 26 cents.  Set your maximum bid on assistant traffic from your own revenue per visit rather than from your search benchmarks, and pull your organic assistant referral baseline before ads reach your market.

Across fifteen tournaments ending in the third quarter, community co-streams took 49.4 percent of the hours while official channels fell 5.4 percent, and the single biggest channel at the biggest Counter-Strike event of the autumn was a Russian streamer on Twitch with roughly 14 percent of the grand final peak.  Ask the events you sponsor for the official-versus-co-stream hours split and price the deal on official hours only until they give it to you.

Eighteen media buyers told Digiday that 10 to 30 percent of Google search budgets are now under review, and the stated reason is that media mix models and geo tests are crediting media at the top of the funnel more and search less.  Find out by name which model your biggest client uses to set channel budget and who owns it, then agree a geo test or holdout on your own video spend before the next planning round.

Fox's advertising revenue rose 47 percent to 2.08 billion dollars and came within 3 million of carriage fees, and Lachlan Murdoch said local stations ran out of availability in the political cycle, which pushes some of the base market aside.  Get the list of your pre-empted spots and value the make-goods today, then move on the rest of November, because the availability comes back when the polls close tonight.

Glen And Friends Cooking doubled its median views from 23,940 to 52,268 after announcing on camera that it was dropping most of what it made, moving its aviation videos to a second channel and rebuilding every description with chapters and a question block, and it has no sponsor of any kind.  If you own a food or cookware archive, fund a run of his Old Cookbook Show from your own historical recipe booklets with a written no-veto clause in the first email.
